prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: low-speed head-on collision in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1317; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Officer narrative: On arrival at the intersection, I found two vehicles in a low-speed head-on collision. Driver 1 was operating the northbound sedan and Driver 2 was operating the southbound sedan. A Passenger was seated in the front passenger position of Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 told me of neck and back strain, and the reported symptoms are consistent with the forces expected in a collision of this type. Damage to both front ends matches the impact described by the drivers. Scene photographs confirm several of the reported positions and points of contact. No independent witnesses were located, so the account rests on the statements of those involved and on the physical evidence. I confirmed through my observations and through statements at the scene that the Passenger was in the vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 1 advised that the vehicle had no prior damage to my knowledge, and I observed no signs of earlier repairs. Driver 1 stated that they reside in the same household as the named policyholder, and that the policyholder's household members are generally covered under the policy. No citations were issued at the scene.
